'''Isachi-no-Sukune''' (''isachi no sukune'') was a {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. In the Empress Jingū regency chronicle of the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}'' he is written as '''Isachi-no-Sukune'''; in the ''{{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}}'' as '''Isachi-no-Atai'''; and in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' as '''Isahi-no-Sukune'''.

== Overview ==
In both the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}'', he appears as the general Isachi-no-Sukune (''isachi no sukune'', Isahi-no-Sukune){{efn|Ancestor of the {{ill|Kishi|ja|吉師}}: it is unclear whether this is the same clan as the Naniwa Kishi subordinates who danced the {{ill|Kishi-mai|ja|吉志舞}} together with the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏}}.}} who, together with {{ill|Kuramiwake-no-Ōkimi|ja|倉見別王}}, the ancestor of the {{ill|Takebe clan|ja|建部氏}}, sided with {{ill|Prince Kagosaka|ja|麛坂皇子}} and {{ill|Prince Oshikuma|ja|忍熊皇子}} and fought against {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}. After being defeated in battle, the ''Kojiki'' states that he went out to sea and composed a poem together with Prince Oshikuma before drowning in the sea, while the ''Nihon Shoki'' states that he composed a poem together with Prince Oshikuma and sank at the Seta crossing.

Based on the descriptions in both books, Isachi-no-Sukune is considered to have committed suicide at this point, but in the Empress Jingū regency chronicle of the ''Nihon Shoki'', by Empress Jingū's command, {{ill|Wakahirume-no-Mikoto|ja|稚日女尊}} was enshrined at Ikuta-Nagasa-no-Kuni.

The ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'' {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} makes him the ancestor of the {{ill|Munasashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|胸刺国造}}.

The "50" (''i'', ''ito'', ''iso'', etc.) part of the name appears in old names connected to the imperial family, but its meaning is unclear.

== Genealogy ==
His father was {{ill|Etamohi-no-Mikoto|ja|兄多毛比命}}, the first {{ill|Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|武蔵国造}}. His brothers include {{ill|Ōshika Kuni-no-Atai|ja|大鹿国直|qid=Q97706278}}, the first {{ill|Kikuma no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|菊麻国造}}; Ana-Yamato-Ko-no-Atai, the first {{ill|Ōshima no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|大島国造}}; and Ōyagi-no-Sukune, the first {{ill|Hōki no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伯岐国造}}.
